reasoning: Base-rates lane, round 2. Supervisor findings taken: Westerman is ~$160M revenue (424B5) bought for ~$116M, so it leaves the core years and enters at cost; the 14x cross-check was a peer median for a stream that ends by 2030, now a finite-life 5.0x from annuity arithmetic (Orano agreement through 2030 per the 10-K); HALEU at $380/SWU (DOE option $17.0M/MTU = ~$415 only if feed is supplied); and my option leg now uses the rNPV's own capex ($1,477/SWU-yr), deck and 0.675 probability, so the expansion option is worth ~$3.7/share instead of ~$17. DOE milestones are discounted at 5.5% (government payer) with my own phase probabilities ($609M). (1) Price base rate: LEU's annual log returns 2021-26 have sd ~1.0 and realised vol is 89%; an efficient-market forecast has a median ~15% below spot (mean ~spot x 1.10, sd 0.75), so P(up) ~0.40 before any view. (2) Positioning: ~30% of float short (mild negative per Asquith-Pathak-Ritter, but squeeze risk), a -71% year, and LEU's own history of violent rebounds (2025: $54 -> $400). (3) Events: December hike ~74-77% priced (Kalshi/Polymarket), the 2028 Russian ban is law, the company lock-up ends ~11-08 and a raise is 40% likely. (4) Project base rates: 1 of 4 US enrichment new-builds of 2004-12 reached operation; ACP halted at this site in 2009. At ~$1,477/SWU-yr, $215/$380 SWU and a 45% margin the initial build is NPV-negative unrisked; value rests on net cash, Westerman, the DOE-funded HALEU milestones and the abandonment option: engine fair value $45.52 (bear $29.60, bull $62.16), versus $59.02 in round 1. (5) Ladder: 80% weight on the efficient-market lognormal (median $93, sd 0.75) and 20% on my research distribution (median $44, sd 0.55): median ~$79, mean ~$109, P(>= $109.88) 0.339. The key judgment remains the undisclosed capex; at Orano-level cost my value would be ~$75-80.

model_inputs.structure_note: Centrus is a finite fuel-cycle resale book (TENEX + Orano SWU) funding a first-of-a-kind US centrifuge build-out. The engine's 3 years are the CORE book only (LEU trading + Technical Solutions; Westerman now valued at cost as an equity adjustment instead of sitting in the years), GAAP EBIT before build-out growth costs; the core runs off after Russian imports are barred on 2028-01-01 (FY2028 -23.7%) and the fixed DCF fades from that run-off level. All build-out spend from 2026-07-01 and its cash flows sit in one rNPV programme in 'adjustment' mode (initial ~1.49M SWU incl. 12 tU/yr HALEU, $215/$380 SWU, 45% margin, p 0.675, $2.2B spend) with the DOE task-order milestones as milestones_pv at a 5.5% government-payer rate. Value is carried by the DCF (0.40, engine) and two custom legs built from the SAME capex, price and probability inputs as the rNPV (market-share states 0.25; cash floor + real options 0.25); EV/EBITDA at a finite-life 5.0x is a 0.10 cross-check (method_fit cap). Reverse DCF is a 0-weight check.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) initial build-out spend $2.2B from 2026-07-01 (~$1,477/SWU-yr; undisclosed, 'multi-billion'): at Orano-level cost fair value rises ~$30-35/share, the largest single swing; (2) SWU deck $215 LEU / $380 HALEU and a 45% cash margin; (3) success probability 0.675 (US 2004-12 enrichment wave: 1 of 4 projects reached operation); (4) 40% chance of a ~$400M raise before the horizon (the company lock-up ends ~2026-11-08). Option leg (e) values the abandonment flexibility the committed rNPV ignores (initial-build call $420M vs intrinsic $104M): it is why (e) sits ~$5/share above (b); the expansion adds only ~$3.7/share because at my own capex it is NPV-negative. Converts: 2.25% 2030 notes ($97.50) in the money, principal in cash, ~0.47M net shares included; 0% 2032 notes and the common warrants ($226.86-$362.98) out of the money. Defense adjacency (Kilian's rule): ~0% of FY2026-28 revenue; Antares (Army Janus / Air Force microreactors) and 'unobligated' HALEU for national-security missions could be ~5-10% of the HALEU programme's value in the 2030s (<$1/share at my HALEU value) - flagged, not excluded. I differ from the supervisor on: the cross-check multiple (5.0x from a finite-life annuity, not 6.0x), the raise probability (0.4 not 0.5), DOE milestone probabilities (mine 0.90/0.70/0.675, tied to the build's own phases) and the thesis break ($38 not $40).
